questions.q: When did an Indian rocket first put a satellite into orbit, which rocket was it, and how heavy was the satellite?
questions.do: Tap the first green dot on the SLV-3 row of Every flight since 1979, or read The road from Thumba.
questions.a: 18 July 1980, on SLV-3: the 35 kg Rohini RS-1. The first SLV-3 flight, in 1979, had failed.

questions.q: Which Indian rocket has never failed so far, and how many times has it flown?
questions.do: Read the right-hand ends of the lines in Learning to fly.
questions.a: LVM3: 100% over 9 flights, including Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3.

questions.q: How many satellites did PSLV-C37 carry in 2017, and how does the page check that number?
questions.do: Search C37 in The launch log, then read How far to trust it.
questions.a: 104 satellites. The page counts them from the payload list (one Cartosat-2D, the small satellites and 88 + 8 Doves and Lemurs), and the count matches the published record.

questions.q: A rocket can lift much less to a high orbit than to a low one. How much can LVM3 carry to low orbit and how much to GTO?
questions.do: Read the LVM3 bars in How much each rocket lifts.
questions.a: 10,000 kg to low orbit but 4,200 kg to GTO, well under half. Climbing higher costs far more speed, so the payload must shrink.

questions.q: Why was India’s first rocket station built at Thumba, and what did the local church give?
questions.do: Read the first entry of The road from Thumba.
questions.a: Thumba lies very close to Earth’s magnetic equator, ideal for studying the upper atmosphere. The church gave its prayer hall and the bishop’s room, and the first rocket, a Nike-Apache, flew on 21 November 1963.
